title: Attention Tiler & Arch-Aware Kernel Compactor for Mixed-Prefill Workloads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's runtime currently selects kernels largely at operator-level granularity and uses seqlen bucketing for coarse routing. For mixed-prefill workloads we observe suboptimal attention throughput because the chosen attention kernel assumes a tile/stripe shape that is inefficient on some architectures (e.g. A100 vs H100) and for variable QKV memory layouts. This ticket pilots an approach that (1) automatically generates a small catalog of attention tile configurations via targeted microbenching, (2) compacts/merges equivalent kernel code-paths where the tiling differences are small (reducing binary permutations), and (3) integrates a lightweight runtime decision rule that switches tiling/variant at the prefill->decode boundary when beneficial.

Goals / Success criteria:
- End-to-end latency reduction for mixed-prefill workloads: 5–15% p50 and 10–25% p95 improvement for targeted models (e.g., 7B–70B families) on H100 and A100 families.
- No more than 5% increase in binary size across supported operator kernels after compaction.
- Fast probe time: microbench probe per model/instance must be < 120s for initial warmstart and < 1s for incremental adjustments.
- Safety: automatic switch must preserve correctness and have an immediate rollback path (per-request fallback to previous kernel).

Constraints and tradeoffs:
- We cannot materially increase per-request scheduling overhead (target < 50us extra).
- Compaction must not reduce debuggability; compiled variant metadata must be traceable back to tile configuration.
- Quantized kernels may behave differently; treat quantized kernels as separate families (no cross-quantization compaction).

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Tile space definition and canonicalization (2w):
   - Define a compact parameterization of attention tiling: (tile_m, tile_n, heads_per_tile, layout_hint).
   - Canonicalize symmetric/rotated tiles to avoid duplicate configs.
   - Produce a deterministic seed generator for microbench runs per model-arch pair.
2) Microbench harness + fast probe (2w):
   - Implement microbench harness that can run in-container on a given GPU with realistic prefills (batch shapes + KV sizes).
   - Prioritize running on limited candidate tile sets using Latin hypercube sampling instead of exhaustive grid.
   - Store compact performance fingerprints in the runtime metadata store (small JSON blobs).
3) Kernel compactor (3w):
   - Static analysis pass to identify near-isomorphic kernel variants with the same code-path except for tiling constants.
   - Generate a merged kernel with runtime-configurable tile parameters where safe (only for FP/AMP kernels; quantized excluded).
   - Ensure symbol naming preserves the original variant mapping for tracing/metrics.
4) Runtime decision rule + switchpoint detection (2w):
   - Implement a lightweight cost model that uses: (arch, seqlen, batch, stored fingerprint) to pick variant.
   - Detect prefill->decode boundary and evaluate expected switch benefit; if > safety threshold and within scheduling budget, switch variant at boundary.
   - Add per-request guardrails: rollback counter and fallback if latency/regression metrics increase.
5) Validation and rollout (2w):
   - Microbench validation across A100/H100 with 7B/13B/70B model artifacts.
   - Internal canary on dedicated pool with 1% traffic, then 10%, monitor p50/p95 and error rates.

Observability and Telemetry:
- New telemetry keys: attention.tile_config, attention.fingerprint_id, probe.latency_ms, variant.switch_decision, variant.rollback_count.
- Dashboard: per-model tile perf surface heatmap by arch and seqlen.
- Automated alert: if rollback_count > 5% over 1h on canary, auto-pause rollout.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalization and seed generator.
- Integration tests that run microbench harness inside CI simulated GPUs (emulation) for correctness.
- Staged canary rollout with A/B trace-level collection and regression detection via existing quality evals.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: microbench mismatch to production workload shapes. Mitigation: collect representative KV size distributions from runtime traces and include them in probe inputs.
- Risk: compaction introduces subtle numerical differences on edge-cases. Mitigation: restrict compaction to FP32/FP16 kernels and build a set of numerical equivalence tests with representative prompts.
- Risk: per-request decision overhead. Mitigation: cache decision per route/model+seqlen bucket and expire on model version or periodic staleness window.

Deliverables:
- Prototype microbench harness + candidate tile catalog (internal artifact).
- Kernel compaction tool and merged kernel binaries.
- Runtime decision rule integrated with scheduler and switchpoint detection.
- Dashboards and telemetry for canary monitoring.

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changes to quantized kernels on the first pass to reduce risk. Future follow-ups should explore quantized-aware tiling and cross-quantized fallback strategies.
